1.why: Screens use a clean sans-serif face at a comfortable size with visibly loose line spacing in body text and labels, though letter-spacing is default rather than expanded.

2.why: No italics or all-caps are used anywhere; every screen has only short sentences and bulleted-style code lists, with no dense paragraphs.

3.why: The single-column card layout with full-width buttons would likely adapt to a phone, but all screenshots are desktop-width (1280px) so mobile rendering, including the wide monospace setup key and log block, is unverified.

4.why: Most instructions are one short plain sentence (e.g. 'Enter the six-digit verification code.'), though lines like 'Your password confirms ownership separately from the demonstration verification code.' are abstract wording.

5.why: No placeholder or worked example of an expected entry is shown for the verification code, authenticator code or recovery code fields; only a description ('six-digit', 'Type: Time-based, 6 digits') is given.

6.why: Every step's text is at most two short sentences plus a brief info callout, so nothing long must be read to proceed.

7.why: The 32-character setup key and the eight recovery codes are displayed as static text with no copy button, copy-all, or download option visible, implying manual transcription.

8.why: Step 3 mentions 'scan or manually enter' but step 4 presents only the manual setup key string — no QR code or equivalent scannable alternative appears anywhere.

9.why: Standard email/password fields exist, but there is no visible evidence of autocomplete/one-time-code support, and step 15/16 shows the email and password re-entered manually with no password-manager affordance.

10.why: Each page has a bold heading and one prominent blue primary button, but there is no step indicator (e.g. 'Step 2 of 5') or progress cue to show where the user is in the enrolment flow.

11.why: Nearly every screen asks for a single action with one primary button, though the login screen collects three fields at once and the MFA status page offers two competing buttons plus log out.

12.why: Outcomes are stated plainly ('MFA is active', 'That recovery code has been used and cannot be used again'), but the next required action is usually implied by a button rather than explicitly described.

13.why: 'Show setup key' reveals the secret and 'Generate new recovery codes' re-issues codes, and the failed login can be retried, but there is no hide/re-show option and the recovery codes explicitly 'will not be shown again'.

14.why: The only error observed, 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.', is non-blaming but generic — it names neither the problem nor how to fix it.

15.why: No countdown timers, expiry warnings or session-timeout messages appear on any screen, so reading and entry time is not visibly constrained, although the TOTP code is inherently time-based with no remaining-time indicator.
